report_name: Anthropic Report: AI Models Weaponized for Espionage and Cybercrime

threat_actors.name: Midnight Blizzard
threat_actors.description: A Russian-aligned threat actor that targeted over 20 government and defense organizations across Ukraine and Europe, using the Claude AI model for reconnaissance and crafting sophisticated phishing emails.
threat_actors.goals: Espionage against government and defense organizations.

threat_actors.name: ShinyHunters
threat_actors.description: A cybercrime group whose affiliates used the Claude AI model to automate sifting through data, enabling them to discover and dump 2,100 cloud access tokens across 40 corporate tenants in 34 hours.
threat_actors.goals: Financial gain through the theft and sale of sensitive data.

threat_actors.name: Unnamed Chinese Undergraduates
threat_actors.description: Two university students from China who reportedly created an "exploit foundry" using the Claude AI model to generate over a dozen potential zero-day findings in network appliance firmware within a single month.

threat_actors.name: Unnamed China-based App Studio
threat_actors.description: An application development studio in China that built a network of over 20 dating apps and used the Claude AI model to power more than 4,700 AI personas for large-scale, likely fraudulent, social engineering.
threat_actors.goals: Financial fraud through automated social engineering.

threat_actors.name: Unnamed Yemeni Actor
threat_actors.description: An actor in Yemen documented to have misused the Claude AI model to build rocket guidance software.

threat_actors.name: Mali Spy Agency
threat_actors.description: A Malian intelligence agency that misused the Claude AI model to develop a surveillance system.

attack_patterns.name: Gather Victim Identity Information
attack_patterns.description: Threat actors, such as Midnight Blizzard, used the Claude AI model to automate open-source intelligence (OSINT) gathering to build detailed profiles of targets in government and defense organizations.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: AI models like Claude were used to generate highly convincing and context-aware phishing emails at scale for espionage campaigns. It was also used to power thousands of AI personas in dating apps for large-scale social engineering.

attack_patterns.name: Obtain Capabilities: Vulnerabilities
attack_patterns.description: Chinese undergraduates used the Claude AI model to analyze network appliance firmware and generate over a dozen potential zero-day findings, effectively automating vulnerability research.

attack_patterns.name: Develop Capabilities: Malware
attack_patterns.description: Threat actors used the Claude AI model for writing custom malware, scripts, and tools, as well as automating malware reconstruction to evade antivirus detection.

attack_patterns.name: Automated Collection
attack_patterns.description: Affiliates of the ShinyHunters group used the Claude AI model to automate the process of sifting through data to discover and collect cloud access tokens from corporate tenants.

attack_patterns.name: Obtain Capabilities: Generative AI
attack_patterns.description: Threat actors obtained and misused generative AI capabilities from the Claude model to assist in various stages of their operations, including reconnaissance, social engineering, and exploit development.

attack_patterns.name: Develop Capabilities
attack_patterns.description: Actors in Yemen and Mali used the Claude AI model to develop capabilities for rocket guidance software and a surveillance system, respectively.

tools.name: Claude
tools.description: A family of large language models from Anthropic that was systematically misused by various threat actors to enhance cyber operations, including espionage, exploit development, and social engineering.

identities.name: Government and Defense Organizations
identities.description: A class of over 20 organizations in Ukraine and Europe targeted by the Russian-aligned Midnight Blizzard group in an AI-assisted espionage campaign.

identities.name: Corporate Tenants
identities.description: A class of 40 corporate cloud tenants from which ShinyHunters affiliates exfiltrated 2,100 cloud access tokens using AI to automate data analysis.

identities.name: Dating App Users
identities.description: A class of 25,000 users who interacted with over 4,700 AI personas on a network of dating apps, likely for fraudulent purposes.

infrastructure.name: AI-Powered Dating App Network
infrastructure.description: A network of over 20 dating apps created by a China-based studio, which used the Claude AI to power over 4,700 AI personas for large-scale social engineering and likely fraud.

indicators.name: Anomalous Claude AI API Usage
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Claude AI API Usage
id: 2b9a1c3d-f4e5-4b6c-8a9b-0d1e2f3a4b5c
status: experimental
description: Detects anomalous patterns of API usage to Anthropic's Claude AI, which could indicate misuse for cyber operations such as reconnaissance, phishing content generation, or code generation.
references:
  - https://cyberscoop.com/anthropic-report-ai-enabled-cyber-attacks/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-11
tags:
  - attack.t1588.007
  - atlas.aml.t0016.002
level: low
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    cs-host: 'api.anthropic.com'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate use of the Claude API for benign purposes.
indicators.description: Detects API calls to api.anthropic.com. While not inherently malicious, a high volume of requests or requests originating from unusual sources could indicate misuse of the AI model for malicious purposes as described in the Anthropic report.
